- How would you handle fragmentation over time?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests fundamentals of low-level synchronization, memory ordering, and cache performance with a simple, fair mechanism that beginners can implement and reason about.

## Key Concepts
- Atomic operations and memory_order semantics
- Fairness via ticketing
- False sharing and cache-line padding
- Simple microbenchmarks to compare contention behavior

## Code Example
```javascript
// Pseudo-C: structure and lock/unlock in C with atomics
#include <stdatomic.h>
typedef struct { alignas(64) atomic_uint64_t next_ticket; atomic_uint64_t now_serving; } ticket_lock_t;
void lock(ticket_lock_t *l){ uint64_t t = atomic_fetch_add(&l->next_ticket,1); while (atomic_load(&l->now_serving) != t) {} }
void unlock(ticket_lock_t *l){ atomic_fetch_add(&l->now_serving,1); }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you modify for multiple locks to reduce contention?
- How would you detect and fix starvation in adversarial workloads?
